hypothesis: CB2-dependent activity is reproducible for identity-resolved β-caryophyllene.
validation_design: Human CB2 binding plus cAMP/β-arrestin concentration-response, then primary human monocytes.
critical_controls: CB2 antagonist or knockout; CB1 counter-screen; vehicle; positive CB2 ligand; purity and stereochemical identity.
decision_rule: Support only if CB2 potency and the named cellular endpoint replicate with antagonist/genetic confirmation.

hypothesis: Free β-myrcene activates or modulates human TRPV1 concentration-dependently.
validation_design: TRPV1-expressing and knockout/non-expressing cells with calcium and patch-clamp concentration-response.
critical_controls: Capsazepine; capsaicin; vehicle; free-compound solubility; cytotoxicity; matched vehicle.
decision_rule: Support only for a TRPV1 assay signal if the response is TRPV1-dependent and not cytotoxicity or formulation artifact.

hypothesis: Free nerolidol interacts with TRPV1 under defined assay conditions.
validation_design: Repeat the inducible human-cell TRPV1 assay using identity-resolved free nerolidol across a concentration series.
critical_controls: TRPV1 knockout; capsazepine; free versus nanoparticle formulation; cytotoxicity; vehicle.
decision_rule: Do not assign nanoparticle activity to free nerolidol without formulation-matched confirmation.

hypothesis: Linalool modulates defined GABAA receptor subtypes and changes neuronal excitability.
validation_design: Recombinant GABAA electrophysiology followed by a neuronal network preparation.
critical_controls: Bicuculline/picrotoxin; flumazenil; diazepam; inactive subtype controls; oxygenated metabolite panel.
decision_rule: Report subtype, direction, EC50/Emax, and exposure context; do not label human anxiolysis or sedation from this alone.

hypothesis: (-)-α-pinene modulates GABAA signaling more strongly or differently than (+)-α-pinene.
validation_design: Compare enantiopure compounds in recombinant human GABAA subtypes and hippocampal-slice electrophysiology.
critical_controls: Flumazenil; picrotoxin; zolpidem; vehicle; racemate; concentration and purity checks.
decision_rule: Support only a stereoisomer- and assay-specific mechanism if the enantiomer difference replicates.

hypothesis: Borneol enantiomers produce distinct GABAA activity and GABAA-dependent behavioral effects.
validation_design: Enantiopure recombinant GABAA electrophysiology followed by a blinded animal study with PK.
critical_controls: Bicuculline; flumazenil; isoborneol; camphor; motor-function and sedation controls.
decision_rule: Behavioral translation requires receptor confirmation, antagonist sensitivity, and exposure measurement.

hypothesis: α-bisabolol inhibits α7-nAChR and separately produces an α7- or GABAA-linked immune/neural phenotype.
validation_design: α7 patch clamp plus immune-cell cytokine assay, with a separate GABAA behavioral/mechanistic study.
critical_controls: α7 antagonist/knockdown; nicotine/choline; GABAA counter-screen; flumazenil; vehicle; viability.
decision_rule: Keep α7 and GABAA mechanisms as separate claims unless a direct causal bridge is demonstrated.

hypothesis: Limonene enantiomers have distinct receptor, inflammatory, or neuronal activity profiles.
validation_design: Identity-resolved d-, l-, and racemic panel across the same receptor/cellular assay battery.
critical_controls: Enantiomer purity; oxidation-product controls; matched vehicle; positive and negative controls.
decision_rule: A null result narrows the evidence map; it does not disprove broad promotional claims.

hypothesis: Reported antimicrobial or antioxidant signals are reproducible for isolated compounds.
validation_design: Standardized MIC/MBC testing and orthogonal cell-free antioxidant assays.
critical_controls: Positive/negative controls; solvent; growth-independent viability; redox-interference controls; purity.
decision_rule: Report endpoint-specific activity only; do not infer a human receptor mechanism.
